## The lost plants of the W̱SÁNEĆ/Saanich Peninsula

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="lost"}
This gallery shows `<span class="mxcw-lost-count">@{count}</span>`{=html} native species once reported for the Saanich Peninsula, which have not been seen in recent decades. Some may be lost *to us*—overlooked, forgotten, or waiting to be rediscovered. Others may be lost *because of us*, through impacts like habitat change or the introduction of invasive species.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Select a plant from the gallery</span> to read its curatorial notes, then explore its distribution on the [Atlas](#pane:Status), or add curatorial notes in [Living Data](#pane:Curation). Then join local naturalists and community members on a search for the
[“Lost” Plants of the Saanich Peninsula](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/lost-plants-of-the-saanich-peninsula)
project on iNaturalist.
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="confirmed" hidden="hidden"}
These native species were reported for the peninsula in the past, and have been seen again since 2000. They represent the enduring core of its native flora—though being found again is no promise of security, and some plants are known to occur in only one or two places.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Select a plant from the gallery</span> to read its curatorial notes, then explore its distribution on the [Atlas](#pane:Status), or add curatorial notes in [Living Data](#pane:Curation).
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="new" hidden="hidden"}
These native species were first reported for the Saanich Peninsula since 2000. Some were surely here all along, overlooked by earlier botanists or confused with their relatives; others may be new arrivals or newly recognized taxonomically.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Select a plant from the gallery</span> to read its curatorial notes, then explore its distribution on the [Atlas](#pane:Status), or add curatorial notes in [Living Data](#pane:Curation).
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="excluded" hidden="hidden"}
Not every plant reported for the peninsula is an accepted part of its flora. Some plants have been excluded for various reasons: curators have judged some to be doubtful records, others to be garden escapes that persist without establishing, or to have been planted.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Select a plant from the gallery</span> to read curatorial notes.
:::

::: {.mxcw-lost-text data-gallery="underReview" hidden="hidden"}
These taxa are under review, and are not yet on the checklist. Plants are evaluated and prioritized for review based on the weight of evidence.

<span class="mxcw-callout">Select a plant from the gallery</span> to read curatorial notes.
:::

:::: {.mxcw-footnote}
Szczawinski and Harrison’s (1972) *Flora of the Saanich Peninsula* provides the historical baseline for this atlas. Harvey Janszen devoted
much of his life to revising this flora, but passed away in 2021, before completing this work. A community of naturalists has
since carried those efforts forward; this atlas is a testament to that continuing legacy.
::::
